status: frozen 2026-10-18 (Slice 5C.2) from the owner's decisions on the Slice 5C.1 development findings (funding infeasibility, seasonal backlog reference, clustered breaches, transition classification), before any primary strategy is chosen; pending one independent review of the corrected framework before the holdout is unsealed
effective: every evaluation from engine 0.2.0-dev.13 on; v0.2-eval-2 is superseded; its development reports (Slice 5C.1) are kept unchanged
notes: Rationale for every value: docs/evaluation/README.md; each rule changed from v0.2-eval-2 is listed in changes. Each change corrects a requirement shown structurally infeasible or statistically misspecified, from the model's own structure (payment cycles, the scenario's season factors, the day and week structure of the run) and synthetic operating characteristics (docs/evaluation/oc-v0.2-eval-3.json), never from a candidate's rank.

Unchanged: the breach gates (urgent 12%, soon 32%, routine 6%), the joint seed rule and its 10% allowance, evidence minimums, case selection, solvency, T90 as the primary financial endpoint, and every other threshold of v0.2-eval-2. Every threshold is compared exactly (integer cross products in basis points).

backlog.legacyRule: historical (plan D README): mean backlog at the day-180 sample at most 1.1 times the mean at the day-90 sample; single samples on different weekdays. Reported for comparison, never gated.

verdict: INVALID: any record, comparison or evaluation integrity check fails (README §10). An invalid evaluation is not evidence; fix and rerun.

NO GO: any hard gate fails or lacks evidence: service (the joint seed rule over every per-seed gate of the gated windows, and every gated pooled rate), case selection (every failing stratum, and every blocking stratum lacking evidence), backlog (workload-adjusted block checks, absolute stale and persistent checks), solvency (cash after every posting at or above the floor, nothing past due) and funding (the dated settlement test: every obligation recognized by the horizon paid when due within the observation, and cash at the end of observation covering the committed liabilities outside the recurring payment cycle). The 14-day employee-commitment coverage is reported, never gated.

GO (financial superiority): every hard gate passes; the plan's own mean operating profit is positive at T90 and at T180; the T90 paired 95% interval of incremental operating profit is above zero; and T180 validation holds (its joint seed rule and pooled rates pass, and its mean increment is positive).
CONDITIONAL GO (relative improvement): every hard gate passes and the mean T90 increment is positive without every GO condition; the missing conditions are listed.

CONDITIONAL GO (transition, not yet repaid): every hard gate passes, the mean T90 increment is not positive, and the mean increment over the operating window (days 31-90) is positive: a solvent, clinically eligible reorganization that has not repaid its transition cost by T90. T180 profit and payback are reported, never promoted to financial GO. When the baseline fails service, the service restoration and its T90 cost are also stated.

CONDITIONAL GO (service purchase): every hard gate passes, the mean T90 increment and the operating-window increment are not positive, and the baseline fails the service gates the candidate passes: service restored at the stated cost. A baseline that fails only solvency, funding, backlog or case selection is not a service restoration.
NO GO (no benefit) otherwise: every hard gate passes but there is no T90 increment and the baseline's service already passes.

changes.finding: 5C.1 development: the funding gate failed every plan, no action included, on every seed from day 1
changes.was: no seed's obligations (payables, accrued payroll, severance payable, earned unposted wages, the 14-day forward employee commitment, remote in-flight fees, contract minimums, past due) above its cash at any capture or daily sample
changes.now: cash after every posting at or above the floor through the end of observation (solvency, unchanged), nothing past due at any capture (unchanged), observation through at least settlementDays (31) after the horizon so that every obligation recognized by the horizon falls due and is paid inside the observed run, and at the end of observation cash at least the committed liabilities outside the recurring payment cycle (severance payable, contract minimums, remote in-flight fees, past due). Future receipts are never forecast: only collections the simulation actually makes count. The 14-day employee-commitment coverage is kept as a reported liquidity-risk indicator
changes.rationale: future wages are not payable until the work is done and paid on paydays; counting 14 days of them as payable at every instant required the practice to hold two weeks of payroll beyond everything it already owes, which the no-action practice never does while paying every bill on time. The settlement window is the model's longest recurring payment cycle (payables paid on the 1st for everything accrued before it: at most 31 days; payroll every 14 days)
changes.expectedImpact: plans that pay every obligation when due without negative cash pass; deferral (anything past due), negative cash between samples, truncated observation and unfunded committed liabilities still fail

changes.finding: 5C.1 development: the reference block (days 55-82, Dec 7 - Jan 3) falls in the scenario's December demand low (season factor 0.93; January 1.05), so every later block compared a higher-demand month against it; no action was unstable on 10 of 10 seeds
changes.was: each later block's mean, peak, overdue and exposure within max(10%, floor) of the reference block's
changes.now: the same checks against the reference scaled by the block's observed workload (studies acquired in the block over those acquired in the reference block; Little's law: with stable time in system, backlog is proportional to workload); stale and persistent studies stay absolute (absoluteChecks)
changes.rationale: a seasonal rise in demand raises a stable queue in proportion; it is not instability. Lateness counted a day past due, and persistent studies, are clinically important whatever the demand, so they are never normalized. Only the observed workload of the plan's own blocks is used: no candidate's result
changes.expectedImpact: proportional seasonal growth passes; growth faster than workload, a growing stale burden, persistent studies, spikes and late-tail deterioration still fail. Queues near capacity grow faster than proportionally and can still fail (oc-v0.2-eval-3.json, backlog)

changes.finding: 5C.1 development: soon breaches cluster by week (design effect 1.7-5.9), urgent mildly (1.0-1.3); the dispersion index reached 2-9
changes.was: operating characteristics under independent breaches (and a weekly-correlation Monte Carlo); per-gate dispersion index only
changes.now: per gate, the day (weekday-adjusted) and week design effects of every seed; each pooled rate with a seed-cluster-robust 95% interval (seeds are the independent replicates); the joint rule's failing-seed fraction with its exact one-sided upper confidence bound; operating characteristics under independent, day-clustered, week-clustered and variable-volume models. The thresholds, the joint rule and its allowance are unchanged
changes.rationale: the gates are empirical and assume nothing about independence, but the probability of passing and any confidence statement do: they must be judged under the run's own day and week structure, with seeds as the unit of replication
changes.expectedImpact: no verdict changes by itself; the probability that a plan near a gate passes the holdout is stated without assuming independent patients

changes.finding: 5C.1 development: every reorganization carries $10-24k of transition cost before day 42, so no staffing plan can have a positive T90 increment
changes.was: a plan with no T90 increment was a service purchase (baseline failing service) or NO GO (no benefit)
changes.now: a plan passing every hard gate with no positive T90 increment but a positive mean increment over the operating window (days 31-90) is CONDITIONAL GO, transition not yet repaid; financial GO is unchanged and never granted by T180 results; every comparison reports T90, days 31-90 and T180 absolute and incremental profit, accrual and cash payback, and outstanding transition obligations
changes.rationale: the operating window is the policy's own post-transition window (operatingFromDay 30): a positive increment there distinguishes an unrepaid investment from a standing cost
changes.expectedImpact: solvent, clinically eligible reorganizations are CONDITIONAL GO instead of NO GO when the baseline's service passes; nothing becomes GO

deferredMeasures: Payer and referral-source strata (§13.2): not recorded; a refused patient's payer is never drawn.
Workforce obligations (§13.2, §13.3 DELTA_WORKFORCE): contracted, rostered and worked hours, training, overrun, premium hours, break entitlement and rest deficits.

Access distributions wanted-to-first-booked, wanted-to-current-booked and wanted-to-actual-service for new demand (§13.2); reported instead: booking lead and, for inherited orders, wait past the wanted time.
Contribution by modality and the provisional guarantee shown apart from accrued payroll (§13.2).
Reading-mix coverage-gap exposure and outcome tails by reader kind (§13.2).
Every baseline-relative DELTA_* tolerance of §13.3: none is calibrated or gated.
